accuracy_notes: Each Canary endemic species is classified independently from a government checklist, but the 13 are not independent evolutionary replications.
The seven Canary native controls were individually sourced and are not a complete census of all nonendemic native butterflies.
A missing named HOSTS genus record is not evidence that the butterfly has no larval host in nature.
The 2 Azorean endemics are source-recognized but Hipparchia azorina/azorinus name/rank is unresolved in GBIF.
The unaltered positive GEB 239 model applies to its original known-HOSTS population, not necessarily the full indigenous island fauna.

full_Canary_INBO_present_universe.source: Independent INBO present 33 Canarian butterfly species; exhaustive species-specific regional government BIOTA origin joins
caveats: Regional government labels are sometimes uncertain, especially native probable (NP).
Cacyreus marshalli labeled BIOTA native probable (NP) despite range introduction literature; preserve source-specific classification, sensitivity exclude.
Pieris rapae classified NP in Canary BIOTA but introduced i in historical Madeira checklist; do not transfer origin across islands.
Argynnis pandora and Maniola jurtina mapped to BIOTA subspecies pages; species-rank metadata kept separate.
Purposively searched the HOSTS-unmatched endemic taxa; comparison to other origins is NOT at equal search effort.
Published evidence grades not uniform: first-hand larva, published review, curated natural-history resource.
31/42 is a minimum union of found host-genus reports, not a biological true coverage percentage.
Do not infer resources locally present, effective caterpillar development, colonization, or original GEB generalizability.
